TL;DR: assuming I am vaguely numerate, 1 GW is about 1 part in 450 of total US electricity generation

In 2013 the US produced 4,112 TWh of electricity. Watt hour is a terrible unit (energy divided seconds times by hours). To make it worse this figure is for one year, or in other words energy divided by second times by hours divided by years. So we'll need to crunch some numbers to compare this 1 GW of capacity with total US electricity generation.

Someone please check my calculation:

1 W = 1 J per second.

so with 3600 seconds in an hour,

1 Wh= 3600 J (a unit of energy)

1 year = 3600 (number of seconds in an hour * 24 (no. hours per day) *365 (days per year) = 31536000 s

1 Wh per year = 3600 J per 31536000 s = 0.000114155 W = 1.1 * 10-4 W

1 TW = 1012, or 1 000 000 000 000 W

Given all that, in 2013 the US produced

4112 TWh per year = 4112 * 1012 * 1.1 * 10-4 W = 452 GW

Note: I'm not sure if this code is live right now. The rank formula is the same as when I posted earlier, see the below for the link.

/v/all is ordered by descending rank. To see how it's calculated, you can look at Voat's source code. This goes for your front page as well, applying it only to subverses you're subscribed to.

Skip to the bottom for TL;DR.

Ranking.cs calculates the rank.

public static double CalculateNewRank(double currentRank, double submissionAge, double score) { const double penalty = 1; var newRank = (Math.Pow((score - 1), 0.8)) / (Math.Pow((submissionAge + 2), 1.8)) * penalty; return double.IsNaN(newRank) ? 0 : Math.Round(newRank, 7); }

Written slightly more less-programmatically that becomes (score-1)^0.8 / (age+2)^1.8 * penalty. As I said in an earlier comment, it does this:

  • take the score of the post
  • subtract one from that
  • raise the result to power 0.8. Call the result x.
  • take the submission's age in hours
  • add two hours to the age
  • raise the result to power 1.8. Call this result y
  • calculate x/y
  • multiply the result of this division by "penalty", which is defined to be 1 in the source, it doesn't do anything. Hm, if the precedence in C# is the expected, this multiplication happens last and isn't taken into "y". But as I said, it doesn't do anything since the penalty is 1.
  • If the score happens to be zero or negative (because score-1 will be negative), the raising to power of 0.8 doesn't give an answer, so the code gives rank of zero instead.

Here's also a little sample calculation I made.

TL;DR:

  • If score (result of votes) is less than 2, the post wont show up
  • As a post ages, it's increasingly difficult for its rank to grow
  • New posts appear easily on the all/front page. /edit/ even with low score.
